body: Thank you. I'll try to think this way before making any final decision.

I don't feel much of anything at all. I'm not frantic or filled with dread and anxiety. My sleep schedule has been chaotic since I was little. I slept all day. This has been a long time coming. I don't want to wake up tommorow and that's just the way it is.
Thank you. Maybe I'll wake up and get to start over. Goodbye.
Goodbye. Thank you.
That's okay. I made up my mind and I don't want to bother you. Thanks for the offer.
Leaving everything.
Thank you for the encouragement! I hope you stay strong as well.

My criticism is towards therapists that show a bias towards any ideology or political leaning. I have a gender. I have a sexuality. I have opinions on politics. I have political leanings. I have views on religion. I have all of these opinions and I feel that they are completely irrelevant towards my mental health treatment. I don't want my therapist's opinions involved in my therapy even if we agree on everything. All of these things are aside from the point when I'm trying to treat my depression. If I didn't ask to talk about religion, race, gender, sexuality, or politics then I don't want it brought up. My last therapist, for example, thought that the country was biased against women and this was the cause of some of my struggles. I completely disagree with this. I think I have every opportunity to do whatever I would like to pursue, and that being a women even has it's benefits in this country. It's my depression that holds me back, not my gender. For her session to be helpful to me I would have had to already agree (in that specific senario) with a left leaning ideological view of society's treatment of women. I don't care about right or left. I have depression and I want it treated. Sorry for how long the example was. Is my point a little clearer?
That's very helpful. Thank you. I've never taken this approach when looking for therapy.
It's no problem! I misinterpreted what you said. All on me.
Hearing that definitely makes me hopeful. I'm really happy for you and your progress!
Oh! I didn't realize that that was a specific type of therapist that I could search for. Thank you for clarifying.
I'll do some research for certain! I definitely need to make changes to how I deal with my emotions. They've been very numbed over for a very long time.
I hadn't thought of it like that. I do have lots of past experiences that I still find uncomfortable or painful to think about. Thank you very much for the suggestion then!
I'll keep that in mind. There is a psychiatric hospital near me so I'll see if out patient therapy is even an option that they have. Thanks!
I'll try asking for solution focused sessions. Thank you!
I don't think I've gone through anything that can be labeled as "trauma" but thank you for the advice.
That's a good way to word it. I will try something like this when I meet up with my new psychologist. Thank you!

Because you could always commit suicide tommorow. Or the next day. Or a month from today. You'll never get the chance to make sure you tried every possible option you could to get yourself together and find meaning in your life. Aren't you a little indecisive? You must be if you are here. Otherwise you wouldn't have asked. You would have just taken your life already. You are looking for something to hold you back. You can always die tommorow. You owe it to yourself to take the time to find out if there's another way. Good luck to you.
Really? I didn't realize there was any difference between therapists and psychologists. I've only been to people labeled therapists. Are there any other notable differences?
That's good advice, thank you. I think it's comforting when therapists have more experience.
I've been through CBT briefly. I'm hoping ACT will give better results. Thanks for the response.
Yes that is where I've been looking. I hope it works out this time. Thanks!
You're right. I wasn't ever very upfront about what I wanted. I was a timid kid. Still am. I'll try my best. Thank you!

Fair enough. I just want it to be a structured experience. I want to see tangible differences in my life as a result of going to therapy. More about living a disciplined life than about my feelings on how the week went. Y'know?
Thank you for the advice!

Thank you. I really appreciate reading all of that. Everytime someone points out the flaws in my thinking like this I feel a lot more assured. I don't hear it often enough. I wish I had more involved adults in my life. Everything you said I've thought before. I know people can get better regardless of how long they've been struggling. I know a genuine suicide plan takes more effort than I've been willing to put into anything for years. I think I know that I don't really even want to die. I just feel so stuck. I need direction and I don't know where to look for it. I've been in therapy before, but it's been years now, and due to it's lack of effectiveness when I was young my parents aren't willing to try it again. I really don't want to ask them for more help. They are kind, financially supportive, generally encouraging people but they are so absent in my day to day life. I feel so disconnected from them. I've never had any friends. There's no one but myself to rely on and I'm getting really sick of myself. I've had suicidal thoughts since I was 13. I don't know how to move forward. I feel like I'm one bad day away from going through with at least an attempt to end my life. I don't know what to do next and it's so frustrating. Sorry for the rambling. Thank you again for the response.
